Seven JET-ILW deuterium discharges with varying line-averaged density n_e and plasma triangularity δ_u were analyzed.
The L-H transition power threshold P_L-H exhibited a minimum that separated the low and high-density branches, varying by a factor of 2 between 3.4 MW and 6.6 MW.
Gaussian process regression was used to fit the experimental profiles of electron density n_e, electron temperature T_e, and ion temperature T_i.
The low triangularity discharges had lower n_e and larger a/L_ne towards the separatrix compared to the high triangularity discharges.
At ρ_tor = 0.85 and 0.9, trapped-electron modes (TEMs) were dominant at the lowest densities, while ion-temperature-gradient (ITG) modes were dominant at higher densities.
The experimental collisionality range corresponded to a region of minimum linear drive between ITG-TEM and resistive mode branches.
The quasilinear particle flux was directed inward only in the collisionality domain where the linear drive was minimized at ρ_tor = 0.85 for all densities and 0.9 for the highest densities.
QuaLiKiz was found to be inadequate beyond ρ_tor = 0.85, while TGLF-SAT2 agreed well with the GENE linear spectra and quasilinear heat fluxes up to and including ρ_tor = 0.9.

Electromagnetic effects, including finite-β and parallel magnetic fluctuations δB||, were included in the GENE simulations and found to have a typical impact of less than 3% on the ion-scale growth rates.
The effective ion charge Z_eff ranged from 1.2 to 1.4, with all three impurity species (Be, Ni, W) contributing significantly in the low-density branch discharges.
Plasma rotation was not included in most of the simulations due to missing measurements for two out of the seven discharges.
The high triangularity discharges consistently had lower T_e in the pedestal-forming region compared to the low triangularity discharges.
The normalized logarithmic temperature gradients a/L_Te changed little in the pedestal-forming region across the ranges of n_e and δ_u, varying consistently less than 20%.
The high-fidelity Sugama collision operator was used in the GENE simulations, and the impact of finite-Larmor radius effects on the collision operator was found to be negligible.
Numerical equilibria generated with the fixed-boundary ESCO code were used to provide the magnetic geometry for the GENE simulations.
